target: JOOAN JA-A12 / T23N, CV2005/CV2005S1, retained OEM Linux3.10.14 and modules
result: Reserved-memory IVDC workspace lifecycle implemented. Physical allocation/adoption/detach/free completed twice, but only the first cycle was kernel-clean. Stable native capture remains unqualified.

implementation.owner: Global FrameSource channel 0; enable primary first and stop dependent channels first
setup: Cache misc-IVDC direct mode at FS0 CreateChn
Read line count; checked size and page-rounded KSEG0 physical bounds
Require initialized reserved-rmem allocator and rmem descriptor provenance
Checked WB+INV before SET_PADDR; mark possible publication before ioctl
After REQBUFS, require consumed DDR address to equal the reserved allocation
teardown: Track possible queue/start effects even on ioctl errors
Skip STREAMOFF if STREAMON was never attempted; otherwise require it to succeed
Join worker and release queue using REQBUFS(0)
Require consumed DDR address zero, then clear pending SET_PADDR
Close frame FD, check cache maintenance, then free reserved extent
Close cached misc FD at DestroyChn
implementation.failure_retention: Retain allocation/descriptor/FD state on uncertain cleanup; DestroyChn can retry partial EnableChn cleanup. System/ISP teardown refuses unsafe resources.
implementation.stale_process_protection: Check consumed address and Linux TAINT_DIE before ISP startup and first DMA allocation. Another process or DLL reload is not recovery.
implementation.kernel_fault_guard: After the observed repeat-cycle Oops, added TAINT_DIE refusal before workspace setup, allocation/release (including subsequent generic DMA allocations/frees), and global ISP teardown. This guard is fault-injection tested; the damaged-kernel case was not intentionally reproduced again.
implementation.native_encoder: Existing full-NV12 address/size/cache guards remain unchanged; scratch provisioning does not implement native line-ring encoding.

tests.host_t30_suite: Passed; optional T30.so dynamic export check skipped because library is not built
new_tests: Seeded public FrameSource Disable/Destroy/SystemExit retry/retention paths
Fresh allocator refuses stale workspace before opening devices; initialized allocator retains real allocation records/extents after an injected Oops
tests.sanitizers: ASan+UBSan on helper, seeded FrameSource lifecycle and real fake-backed DMA allocation records
tests.mips: Cross-built uClibc library/tool and native contract executables. Final helper (450 checks), FrameSource (385 checks) and DMA contracts passed under QEMU and on the camera CPU using mocked device calls; kernel taint unchanged.
tests.coverage_limits: Seeded lifecycle tests do not invoke the entire EnableChn/capture-worker graph; physical tests exercised successful FS0 enable/disable. No encoded frame was decoded by the focused probe.

assertions.dma: stale initialization, allocation and both address forms of free quarantine

repeat_fault.timing: After both sensors registered and FS0 started, before STREAMOFF on cycle2
repeat_fault.interpretation: Dual registration is necessary but insufficient; secondary activation, initialization or repeated-cycle lifetime remains unresolved. The trace does not identify the exact missing call.

combined_jooanipc_open.result: Stopped before FrameSource at IMP_ISP_Tuning_SetSensorFPS_Sec returning -1. No video readiness; no kernel Oops in this daemon run.

probe_followup: The public probe now rejects an already Oops-tainted kernel and fails when kernel taint changes, rather than treating API return codes alone as qualification.
camera_changes: RAM-only binaries/configuration, process control, necessary SSH reset after kernel Oops; no firmware, boot, module or power-script changes.
